headline: High-risk shared filesystem and git overlap: ECC can write broadly while Copilot edits repo buffers, creating default-path prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ECC can read/write the filesystem, use MCP, and operates on ~/.claude and ~/.cursor/ecc; Copilot reads repo context and editor buffers. That creates a plausible shared-content bridge where one agent can ingest the other's outputs as trusted text. This is not proven by a documented direct channel, so I rate it medium rather than high.
conditions: IF ECC writes instructions or summaries into shared repo files or editor buffers that Copilot reads
IF Copilot Workspace or chat consumes those files as authoritative context without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate ECC and Copilot workspaces
Disable automatic ingestion of generated notes into repo files
Add provenance tags to agent-authored files
Review Copilot Workspace inputs before applying edits

B_data_leakage.rationale: ECC touches session summaries, skills, hooks, git history, and security findings, while Copilot reads repo context and open buffers and sends context to api.githubcopilot.com. If both operate on the same workspace, sensitive ECC-managed material can flow into Copilot's vendor backend. The shared-workspace path is plausible from the profiles, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF ECC stores secrets, findings, or session context in files under the shared repo or editor workspace
IF Copilot is pointed at that same workspace and transmits context to api.githubcopilot.com
mitigations: Keep ECC state outside the repo root
Exclude sensitive files from Copilot context
Rotate or redact secrets before opening the workspace
Use separate OS users or profiles for the two agents

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ECC has unrestricted filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and git-state modification; Copilot can also write filesystem and modify git state in Workspace. Both can mutate the same repo without any locking primitive shown, so concurrent edits and git conflicts are a default danger. The overlap is enough to rate high.
conditions: IF both agents are active on the same repository or branch
IF Copilot Workspace applies edits while ECC is also writing or committing
mitigations: Assign one agent per branch
Pause one agent before the other writes
Require manual git review before commit
Use file-level ownership conventions
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable paths

D_cascading_error.rationale: ECC can generate security findings, documentation, and code changes; Copilot Workspace can apply edits from that context. If Copilot treats ECC output as authoritative, an upstream mistake can cascade into incorrect code or commits. Because the profiles show no verification gate between them, the safer high severity is appropriate.
conditions: IF Copilot Workspace uses ECC-produced text as the basis for edits
IF a human does not independently verify ECC outputs before Copilot applies them
mitigations: Require human review of ECC outputs
Cross-check claims against source files
Limit Copilot to suggestion mode
Keep ECC outputs in non-executable notes

E_compliance.rationale: ECC handles session data, hooks, and security findings with configurable retention, while Copilot is a closed-source vendor service that sends repo context to GitHub. If regulated or sensitive data is placed in the shared workspace, retention and residency expectations can diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific residency breach, so medium fits.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in files visible to both agents
IF organizational policy forbids sending that data to GitHub-hosted services
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces
Redact sensitive fields before Copilot access
Set explicit retention limits for ECC state
Use a compliance-approved environment only
